reason: FEASIBILITY: the idea as proposed (gate-aware loss, 3 um z cap, track-identity pairs, 27-point stencil, 199-video capture) fails on four counts. (1) GPU cost. The head reads the edge-TTA-averaged PRIMARY feature map (ext_x138/DIFF.md l.28), so a capture has to run the full detection and TTA stack. The exp51 log shows about 235-265 s per video per T4, with 2 shards on 2xT4. 199 videos detection-only is about 100 x 250 s = 7 h wall, which is 35% of the ~20 GPU h left. The existing capture mode does not stop after detection: it returns arr unchanged, so ILP and post-processing still run (exp51 took 1,713 s for 4 test videos). Without a new short-circuit patch the 199-video run is over 12 h and breaks the session limit. (2) Disk and code. Capture dumps coords plus 224-d features for EVERY peak, about 30-36k per video: 7-point fp32 is ~32 MB/video (6.4 GB total), and 27-point is ~24 GB, over the 20 GB /kaggle/working limit. New in-kernel code is needed: load the train GT geffs, keep only peaks within 12 um of GT plus a 3% sample, fp16, and stop after detection. Track-identity pairing also needs the final predicted tracks matched to GT. That means either the full pipeline or a mapping of capture peaks to friend A's cache nodes, which may differ at the threshold because the cache came from an RTX 5070 Ti and the capture would run on a T4. (3) The lab cannot measure it. replay.py starts from the POST-GAP ckpt: ILP, motion relink and gap closing are already applied, and raw->ckpt cannot be replayed because DeepCenter has no scores at synthetic gap points. So Step B's coordinate shift only re-runs safe-div, short-track, linefit, div-insert and rounding. The channel through which a head changes swaps and diverted links (edge features at float coords, the kNN candidate set, the ILP, and the relink Hungarian over positions) is invisible. There is no 'port' arm in the cache either, so both arms would be synthetic offsets on cache nodes. On top of that, linefit (w=0.8, window 2) smooths ALL nodes and keeps only ~0.48x of iid per-frame position noise, and the writer and the replay round z to the 1.625 um grid. Much of any extra de-quantisation is erased at the output, so the lab readout is biased toward null and would not predict the LB. (4) Expected value against timeline. The research step already measured the tail offset as unlearnable (|r| <= 0.09; net rescue 43/798), so the gate-aware Step 1 kill test would almost surely fail after ~1.5 GPU h plus the new code. exp51 (the port) is not yet submitted. Deadline is 29 Sep with 5 days left. Other conflicts: a 3 um z cap moves nodes relative to the safe-division geometry gates (2.25 um etc.), DaughterNet insertion (needs ~3 um accuracy) and the edge filter's 'never-scored pair' set, because kNN candidates are rebuilt at the new coordinates. None of this is replayable. Not refuted: shipping itself is easy, because a new state_dict/mean/scale in the same 224->32->3 format is a drop-in for the V1284 file, and a 27-point variant is a small change to sample_features.
fix_if_any: Drop the gate-aware, 3 um cap and track-pairing parts. Keep only a cheap, bounded de-quantiser retrain behind a GT-only kill test that never touches the lab. (a) Add a capture short-circuit to the exp51 kernel. When COORDHEAD_MODE=capture, stop each video after refine(); keep only peaks within 4 um of a GT node (plus a 3% sample); save fp16 7-point and 27-point stencils. (b) Pilot on 36 videos (24 6bba + 12 44b6, one per leak group): about 18 x 250 s = 1.3 h wall on 2xT4 plus ~10 min setup, and under 1 GB of output. (c) On Kaggle CPU, train GroupKFold heads (Huber, pairs < 4 um, 2 um norm-bounded output). Compare them with the public head on the same features, measuring the <4 um share per embryo. Kill unless it improves by >= +0.005 on both embryos. (d) If it survives, do NOT use the ckpt-shift lab as the gate: it cannot see the linking channel. Instead run exp51 with the new head file against exp51 as one LB probe, after exp51 itself has been probed, and with float output decided identically in both arms. Only run the 199-video capture (~7 h) if the 36-video head beats the public head and there is GPU budget left after the probes that are already higher value.
realistic_public_gain: Gate-aware tail version: about 0 (+0.000..+0.0005). The tail is not learnable, and the lab cannot validate it. Plain de-quantiser retrain over the port: +0.000..+0.002 (a guess). Linefit smoothing and z rounding at the output already cap it, and the public head already takes most of the quantisation error. Cost: ~1.5 GPU h for the pilot, ~7 GPU h for a full capture, plus one LB probe.
